_comment: pack-v9: pack-v8's phrasings verbatim, plus what Viva says when she thinks a counterparty may be a standing arrangement rather than a run of separate decisions. Four shapes, kept visibly apart. Where enough of the relationship has been seen to measure a rhythm over one thing, she says what she measured. Where it has not, she says only how many movements there are and what the world says about that kind of business, and makes no claim about a cadence at all. Where there are enough of them to look for a rhythm in and the gaps never settle, she says that too, and asks whether there is simply nothing arranged — which is an answer a person may give, not an absence. And where the movements do not look like one thing — some repeating an amount, the rest not — she says what she saw of each and asks which is which, claiming no cadence over the mixture, because no such thing was measured. The direction is its own sentence, because money out to a counterparty and money back from them are two different arrangements. A released pack is never edited; add pack-v10 instead.
identity: I've read a statement for {account_ref}, but I can't yet tell whose account it is. Is it one you already have with me?
reconciliation_gap: Your {account_ref} statement for {opening_date} – {closing_date} doesn't continue from the balance I hold. A statement in between looks to be missing — do you happen to have one?
reconciliation_gap_why: It opens at {opening_money}; my chain ends elsewhere.
reconciliation_flagged: Your {account_ref} statement didn't add up, so I haven't put it on your books. When you have a moment, could you check the figure I flagged?
reconciliation_held: I'm holding a {doc_type} that didn't reconcile, so its figures aren't on your books yet. Nothing is lost — it is simply waiting for us.
reconciliation_held_for: I'm holding a {doc_type} for your {account_ref} that didn't reconcile, so its figures aren't on your books yet. Nothing is lost — it is simply waiting for us.
transfer: On {date} you moved {money} ({description}). Was that money moving between your own accounts, rather than being spent?
transfer_why: {candidates} movement(s) of the same amount within a few days on another account you hold.
merchant: May I ask what {example} is? You have {count} transaction(s) with it, {money} in total.
merchant_peer_note: (This looks like a payment to a person, so I'll only apply your answer here — not as a rule.)
merchant_why: I don't yet have a category for this merchant.
nature_single: {date}: {description} — {money}. Could you tell me what this one was for?
nature_single_why: The description names how the money moved, not who received it — so I have to ask about each one separately.
nature_group_compound: A payment like that is usually several things at once, and I can't tell the split without the paperwork — I would rather ask than guess.
nature_group_ask: Shall I set that up for you?
nature_group_why: Because of who they are, not because of anything you told me.
nature_group_why_documents: Your {documents} would let me prove it, not just assume it.
corroboration: You've told me about {name} — {money} so far. If you have the {document}, I could prove this rather than just record it. Entirely at your convenience.
corroboration_why: This account exists because you said so; nothing has attested it yet.
corroboration_why_unreliable: Its balance also can't be trusted yet, because part of those payments was interest.
free_text_invite: Tell me in your own words
answered_by_document: This one is answered by the document itself — add it below whenever you have it to hand.
expectation_retirement_flow: Your pay has been setting money aside for retirement — {money} so far — but I've never seen the account it lands in. Do you have a {document}? It would let me show that money growing, rather than just leaving.
expectation_retirement_flow_why: Every pay stub shows the deduction; no statement has ever shown the destination.
expectation_investment_account: You hold {account_name}. Its {document} would tell me what was truly gained or lost — detail I currently have to leave aside. Do you have this year's?
expectation_investment_account_why: Realized gains and dividends of {money} are on your books; the tax form is what attests them.
expectation_account_cadence: My picture of {account_name} ends at {last_date}. A newer statement likely exists — whenever you have it, I'll bring things current.
expectation_account_cadence_why: Nothing is wrong — the account is simply not current, and I would rather say so than pretend.
interview_why: You've told me this one exists; there are just a few things I still need to know about it.
interview_opens: You mentioned there's a {kind_label} against your {name}. Shall we set that one up too, so the two read together?
rhythm_head: I can see {count} movement(s) with {example}, {money} in all.
rhythm_direction_out: That money went out to them.
rhythm_direction_in: That money came in from them.
rhythm_measured: They come round about every {days} day(s), steadily enough that it looks more like one arrangement than a run of separate decisions.
rhythm_measured_fixed: They are for much the same amount each time.
rhythm_irregular: They do not come round on any pattern I can see — the gaps between them keep changing.
rhythm_irregular_ask: Is that right — nothing arranged with them, just as and when?
rhythm_why_irregular: From the dates in your own records rather than what the world does with this kind of business — there are enough of them to look for a rhythm in, and they do not settle into one.
rhythm_mixture_lead: These do not all look alike, so I would rather not read them as one arrangement.
rhythm_mixture_part_repeating: {count} of them are for much the same amount each time, {money} in all.
rhythm_mixture_part_varying: {count} of them vary in amount, {money} in all.
rhythm_mixture_part_lone: And one stands apart from those, for {money}.
rhythm_mixture_ask: Which of those, if either, did you arrange with them, and how often does it come round — and which are separate purchases?
rhythm_why_mixture: Because your records with them do not all look like the same thing, and which is which is yours to say rather than mine to guess.
rhythm_prior_standing: This is the kind of business one usually deals with by a continuing arrangement — set up once, and repeating until it is stopped.
rhythm_prior_either: This is the kind of business one can deal with either way — by a continuing arrangement, or one purchase at a time.
rhythm_prior_period_monthly: Where there is such an arrangement, it usually runs a month at a time.
rhythm_prior_period_annual: Where there is such an arrangement, it usually runs a year at a time.
rhythm_prior_period_either: Where there is such an arrangement, it runs a month at a time about as often as a year at a time.
rhythm_ask: Is that what you have with them, and how often does it come round?
rhythm_why_measured: From the pattern in your own records — I have not taken anyone's word for it, including my own.
rhythm_why_prior: Because of who they are. There is not enough here yet for me to see a pattern of your own, so I am supposing rather than measuring.
